title: Enterprise Resilience
content:
**@gravito/resilience** is the mission-critical reliability engine of the Gravito Galaxy. Known as the **Guardian Layer**, it provides the essential immune system for complex distributed architectures.

Stability Governance: The Immune System

In microservices and satellite architectures, failure is inevitable. The Resilience module doesn't just handle errors—it ensures system stability at the structural level. With these tools, you transform "fragile" synchronous calls into "robust" adaptive links.

1. Circuit Breaker V2

The primary mechanism for preventing cascading failures. Like a fuse in an electrical system, it automatically cuts off connections when downstream services (like third-party payments or databases) become unstable.

Scenario: Third-Party API Latency

When your system depends on an external service like Stripe or AWS, and that service suddenly slows down:

  • Traditional Approach: Requests pile up, leading to Memory Exhaustion (OOM) and a complete crash.
  • Resilience Approach: When failure rates exceed 15%, the Circuit Breaker Opens. Subsequent requests return fallback data or cached values instantly, protecting the main system.
import { CircuitBreaker } from '@gravito/resilience'

const paymentBreaker = new CircuitBreaker({
  failureThreshold: 5,    // Open after 5 consecutive failures
  resetTimeout: 30000,    // Try recovery after 30 seconds
})

// Wrap unstable external calls
const result = await paymentBreaker.execute(async () => {
  return await stripe.charges.create({ ... })
}, { fallback: () => ({ status: 'pending_offline' }) })

2. Adaptive Worker Pools

Leverage Bun's native multi-threading. Resilience provides worker pools that scale dynamically based on real-time event pressure.

Scenario: CPU-Intensive Tasks

Processing image resizing, PDF generation, or heavy encryption on the main event loop will block all HTTP requests.

  • Solution: Dispatch tasks to the WorkerPool. Resilience manages the worker lifecycle and automatically releases memory by pruning idle workers.
import { WorkerPool } from '@gravito/resilience'

const imagePool = new WorkerPool({
  minWorkers: 4,
  maxWorkers: 16,
  script: './img-processor.ts'
})

// Main thread remains fluid; computation runs in background
imagePool.dispatch({ action: 'RESIZE', path: 'avatar.png' })

3. Dead Letter Queue (DLQ)

The final line of defense ensuring that "mission-critical" tasks are never lost.

Scenario: Critical Notifications

If a vital transaction confirmation email fails after 10 retries because the SMTP server is down.

  • Resilience Approach: Instead of throwing an error, the system moves the event and its context to the Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) for manual recovery or later inspection.

4. Backpressure & Load Shedding

An intelligent traffic filtering mechanism based on system health.

Scenario: Traffic Spikes (Flash Sales)

When instantaneous traffic hits 120% of system capacity. Resilience monitors CPU/Memory and performs Load Shedding on low-priority requests (like non-critical logs), ensuring the checkout flow remains stable.

// GALAXY_ADVISORY: FAIL_STRUCTURED

Resilience is not about eliminating errors; it is about "failing gracefully." By deploying guardian patterns, your system maintains predictable behavior even under extreme stress.
